business.objective: Help health policy analysts estimate a country's life expectancy from health, economic and social indicators, and identify which indicators matter most.
business_questions: Which indicators are most strongly associated with life expectancy?
How accurately can life expectancy be predicted for a country the model has never seen?
How uncertain is a single prediction (prediction interval)?
business.data_mining_goal: Multiple linear regression: Life expectancy = f(indicators), with feature selection, evaluated on unseen countries.

situation.resources: One public Kaggle CSV (2,938 rows, 22 columns), Python with scikit-learn and statsmodels.
situation.assumptions: Indicators are comparable across countries and years.
situation.constraints: The model must stay interpretable (linear) for policy discussion.
risks: Many missing values (44% of rows have at least one).
Implausible values (e.g. average BMI above 50) indicate data-entry errors.
Each country appears up to 16 times; a random split would leak the same country into training and testing.
situation.cost_benefit: Cheap to build; useful for prioritising health spending, but associations are not causal effects.

project_plan: Phase 2: profile data, missing values, implausible values, correlations
Phase 3: clean, log-transform skewed variables, split by country, impute (same-country median, then training median)
Phase 4: VIF, feature selection (Lasso, Forward SFS, RFE, ElasticNet), OLS / Ridge / Lasso
Phase 5: test metrics vs success criteria, assumption checks, prediction intervals
Phase 6: deploy only if approved; save model and report

process_review.name: Split by country (no country in both train and test)
Fallback imputation medians computed on training rows only
Feature selection used grouped CV on training data only
Selected model beats the mean-only baseline

next_steps: Proceed to Phase 6 (deployment). Note: Linearity (Ramsey RESET); Homoscedasticity (Breusch-Pagan); Normality of residuals (Jarque-Bera); Independence (Durbin-Watson, by country/year) not satisfied - report cluster-robust standard errors and treat p-values with care.
monitoring_plan: Re-score when WHO publishes a new year of indicators; compare with reported life expectancy.
Retrain yearly, or when the rolling RMSE on new years exceeds 5 years.
Alert when inputs fall outside the training range (data drift).
Check that prediction-interval coverage stays near 95%.
